families.s: HSE explosives security, access and loss-reporting guidance
families.t: unauthorised access, prohibited persons, acquisition, keeping, transfer, civil explosives, relevant explosives, records, losses and plastic explosives
f: Robust security controls should be in place before explosives operations begin.
Security should remain effective for as long as explosives are manufactured, stored or kept.
Controls should prevent unauthorised access.
Transfer restrictions apply to relevant explosives and prohibited persons.
Civil explosives are subject to identification, site-code and record-keeping duties.
Relevant explosive losses must be reported through the required arrangements.
Plastic explosives are subject to marking and possession or transfer restrictions.
Security arrangements should cover people, perimeter, buildings, keys, records, transfers and incident response.
families.g: Security risk depends on explosive category, site and building access, personnel vetting, keys and records, transfer controls, traceability, loss detection, reporting and response.

families.s: HSE civil-explosive identification and traceability guidance
families.t: unique identification, manufacturers, importers, individual items, site codes, record keeping, transfers, loss investigation and supply chain
f: Most civil explosives must carry a unique identification code.
Manufacturers and importers have responsibilities for applying the identification.
Identification requirements vary with the size and form of the explosive item.
Civil explosives should be marked before import into Great Britain where the requirement applies.
Site identification codes support attribution to manufacturing and supply locations.
Records should support tracking through acquisition, transfer, keeping and use.
Traceability assists investigation when explosives are stolen, lost or misplaced.
Records and markings should remain legible, retrievable and linked to the correct items and transactions.
families.g: Traceability effectiveness depends on correct item marking, site codes, importer and manufacturer controls, transaction records, transfer documentation, record retention and loss investigation.

families.s: HSE firework storage, sale and professional-display guidance
families.t: hazard type, net explosive mass, duration, licensing, retail storage, commercial displays, risk assessment, spectators and insurance
f: Firework storage limits depend on hazard type, net explosive mass, purpose and duration.
Larger quantities or more powerful fireworks generally require a storage licence.
Retailers should assess storage and sales arrangements and use suitable separation, fire and access controls.
Commercial displays are work activities covered by health and safety duties.
Display planning should protect workers, spectators and people near the site.
The requirements to store fireworks safely continue even where a limited licensing exception applies.
Professional use of specified high-hazard pyrotechnic categories requires appropriate competence and product-law controls.
Inventory, damaged stock, ignition sources, emergency arrangements and post-display misfires should be managed.
families.g: Firework risk depends on hazard type and net mass, storage duration, building and separation, retail or display activity, weather, spectators, ignition control, competence and emergency arrangements.

families.s: HSE high-nitrogen ammonium-nitrate import, supply and detonation-resistance guidance
families.t: more than 28 percent nitrogen, resistance-to-detonation certificate, import, supply, technical grade, exemptions, storage and enforcement
f: Relevant solid ammonium-nitrate material with more than 28 percent nitrogen is subject to specific controls.
Import and supply generally require a supporting resistance-to-detonation certificate.
The definition also covers certain solid mixtures where nitrogen derived from ammonium nitrate exceeds the threshold.
Specific exceptions exist for some users of technical-grade ammonium nitrate.
Storage for on-site manufacture of explosives may be permitted only under the applicable authorisation or exemption.
Import, storage and keeping outside the general route may require an HSE exemption certificate.
Documentation should establish composition, nitrogen content, certificate status, supplier and intended use.
Security, segregation, contamination prevention and inventory control remain important alongside supply-law compliance.
families.g: High-nitrogen ammonium-nitrate risk and compliance depend on composition, nitrogen percentage, physical form, certificate or exemption, storage, contamination, security, quantity and intended use.

families.s: HSE offshore safety-case and major-accident-risk demonstration guidance
families.t: production and non-production installations, external waters, safety case, design notification, material change, risk assessment, verification and thorough review
f: Offshore safety-case legislation aims to reduce major-accident risks to the workforce.
Production operators, non-production installation owners and well operators can have safety-case duties.
The 2015 safety-case regime applies to covered oil and gas operations in external waters.
The safety case should demonstrate that major-accident risks are identified and effectively controlled.
Specified submissions can include design notifications, material changes and thorough reviews.
Risk assessment and verification arrangements support the safety-case demonstration.
Decommissioning and dismantling require continued verification and risk control.
Ageing installations require structured review of integrity and life-extension arrangements.
families.g: Safety-case adequacy depends on installation and operation type, major-accident scenarios, risk assessment, management systems, verification, design and change submissions, ageing and review.
